output.summary: The rise in ED length of stay for admitted patients is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 hours), and system timestamps show it began in March. Boarding jumped when medical-ward discharges moved later after the hospitalist rounding change. Surgical wards did not change. Bed capacity, occupancy and inpatient length of stay are flat, and ED arrivals and admissions do not differ between huddle and non-huddle days. The ED work-up interval barely moved, so nurse understaffing is not supported as the main cause. Door-to-provider and left-without-being-seen worsening is plausibly a boarding effect and the May triage-provider cut, which is not separated yet. Cleaning cuts began in September and boarding was already high. Extend the huddle and avoid the travel-nurse contract.
